title: Less Small Examples
description: Use these small Less examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Build your first Less file
examples.description: Less is a CSS helper language. A compiler translates its extra features into the CSS that browsers already understand.
examples.output: Less is added to the project. The version command confirms that the tool can run.

examples.title: Store a colour in a name
examples.description: Less variables start with @. A variable lets you reuse a value such as a colour or a spacing size.
examples.output: Both rules have navy as their text colour after compilation.

examples.title: Nest child styles
examples.description: A nested selector chooses an element inside another element.
examples.output: The built CSS contains a .card p rule. It removes margins from paragraphs inside cards.

examples.title: Style the current element
examples.description: The & sign repeats the parent selector. It helps add a state to the same element rather than choosing one of its children.
examples.output: The CSS contains .button:hover and .button:focus-visible rules for the button itself.

examples.title: Reuse a mixin
examples.description: A mixin is a group of style choices you can insert into another rule.
examples.output: Both card and tip get the two style choices. No separate soft-box rule is needed.

examples.title: Pass a mixin value
examples.description: A mixin can accept a value, so one recipe makes several kinds of frame.
examples.output: The book has a navy border and the game has a green border.

examples.title: Calculate space
examples.description: Less can calculate a size from other sizes.
examples.output: The result uses 12px padding and 28px margin.

examples.title: Split a style file
examples.description: An import brings another Less file into the build.
examples.output: With both files in one folder, the built h1 rule uses navy.

examples.title: Guard a recipe
examples.description: A guard is a rule that decides whether a mixin should run.
examples.output: The h1 rule gets a bold weight because 24px is at least 20px.

examples.title: Change a colour value
examples.description: Less has colour functions. A function takes a colour and calculates another colour from it.
examples.output: The background uses a lighter version of the base colour. The text uses a darker version.

examples.title: Insert a name into a selector
examples.description: Interpolation puts a variable value inside a selector name.
examples.output: The output selector is .garden-card. It has a green border.

examples.title: Combine a card and a screen rule
examples.description: A media query chooses styles for certain screen sizes.
examples.output: Cards get more inner space when the viewport is 640px wide or wider.
